item.text:
`src/pyocd_debug_mcp/kernel/processes.py` has the CL-004 repair in place.

What changed:
- `process_group_options(platform="nt")` now falls back to the real Windows creation-flag values, so it returns `0x00000204` even when the host lacks `subprocess.CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` / `CREATE_SUSPENDED`.
- Windows `ctypes` access is centralized behind a small local lookup boundary.
- `_create_windows_kill_job()`, `_resume_windows_process()`, `_close_windows_job()`, and `_windows_start_token()` now use that boundary.
- Missing Windows APIs raise contextual `OSError` instead of pretending the call succeeded.
- POSIX session/process-group behavior, cleanup phases, deadlines, marker lifecycle, primary exception identity, and public signatures are preserved.

Checks run:
- `python -m py_compile src/pyocd_debug_mcp/kernel/processes.py`
- `git diff --check -- src/pyocd_debug_mcp/kernel/processes.py`
- `uv sync --locked` in a separate temp `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT`

- `uv run --locked --no-sync ruff check src/pyocd_debug_mcp/kernel/processes.py`
- `uv run --locked --no-sync pytest tests/test_process_cleanup.py -q`
